title: CRITICAL: prove keyboard input reaches AVM1 in published SWFs (Key.isDown e2e)
description: RESOLVED — keyboard input DOES reach AVM1; the prior 'headless Ruffle can't drive keyboard' claim was false. Proof: apps/desktop/e2e/keyboard.spec.ts publishes a SWF with onClipEvent(keyDown){ _root.gotoAndStop(2); } over a red(frame1)/blue(frame2) background, clicks the Ruffle player to focus it, then page.keyboard.press('ArrowRight'), and asserts the stage flips red->blue. Command: pnpm --filter @flash/desktop e2e --grep 'keyboard input reaches AVM1'. Result: 1 passed; logs: before red=10000 blue=0; focus state docHasFocus=true activeIsHost=true; after red=0 blue=10000; red->blue pixelDiff=10000. KEY FINDINGS: (1) FOCUS is the load-bearing step — Ruffle gates its window keydown handler on an internal has_focus flag set via focusin on the <ruffle-player> host; a real .click() is required. (2) autoplay:'on' + unmuteOverlay:'hidden' needed so clip ticks start in headless (default auto + suspended AudioContext shows a play button and never calls play()). (3) headless Chromium's no-GPU hardware-accel overlay must be hidden before screenshots. (4) Key.isDown(n)/Key.getCode() are BROKEN in the bundled Ruffle 0.1.0 headless build — they return false/0 even inside the keyDown handler; the keyDown EVENT itself is the reliable proof. (5) Side-finding: AS2 compiler mis-compiles member-target assignment (this._x = v / obj.prop += v) as a GetMember read instead of SetMember write — bare _x = v works. Findings documented in CLAUDE.md.
